Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Chad has moved toward digital public revenue collection: PwC notes that under the E.Tax platform, certain taxpayers must pay taxes via bank transfer/electronic payment, and Financial Afrik reports a 2025 circular prohibiting cash collection of state revenues by revenue agencies. Evidence: [PwC Tax Summaries – Chad significant developments](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/chad/corporate/significant-developments); [Financial Afrik – Chad opts for digital payments of public revenues](https://www.financialafrik.com/en/2025/09/10/chad-state-opts-for-digital-payments-of-public-revenues/).

Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: Chad has an operational eTax portal/platform enabling online filing and payment: Africa24 reports official launch (Jan 2023) of e-Tax teledeclaration/telepayment; PwC Tax Summaries references ‘E.Tax platform’ for online filing and electronic payment; DGI’s official video links to the platform URL (sigi.finances.gouv.td). Evidence: [Africa24 TV – launch of e-Tax teledeclaration/telepayment](https://africa24tv.com/tchad-lancement-de-la-teledeclaration-et-du-telepaiement-en-ligne); [PwC Tax Summaries – Chad significant developments](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/chad/corporate/significant-developments); [YouTube – DGI Tchad tutorial referencing platform URL](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Me_EmV3V1ss).

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: People-to-government payments are available in limited form (tax payments via mobile/online). Evidence: World Bank PAD notes project will support G2P and P2G payments delivered by mobile money, and PwC Tax Summaries notes taxpayers under normal regime required to pay taxes by bank transfer/electronic payment; Africa24 reports launch of e-Tax teledeclaration/telepayment and mobile payment of IGL tax. Evidence: [Africa24 TV (télédéclaration/télépaiement e-Tax; IGL via mobile)](https://africa24tv.com/tchad-lancement-de-la-teledeclaration-et-du-telepaiement-en-ligne); [PwC Tax Summaries – Chad significant developments (E.Tax platform, electronic payments)](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/chad/corporate/significant-developments)

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Chadian law does not provide a mandatory data breach notification protocol (noted explicitly in DLA Piper’s Chad summary). Evidence: [DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – Chad](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=TD).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022 reports that for CEMAC (which includes Chad), “none of the countries in the CEMAC region have a national IPS”; Chad is not listed among domestic IPS systems live as of June 2022, but Chad participates in the regional interoperable retail payment switch GIMACPAY (launched July 2020) that provides domestic + cross-border instant clearing across CEMAC. Evidence: [AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022 report](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/EN_SIIPS_Report_web.pdf); [AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 CEMAC case study](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/SIIPS2023_CaseStudy_CEMAC.pdf)

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: World Bank PAD for Chad Digital Transformation Project states “Only 0.1 percent of adults receive government payments in digital form,” indicating extremely low digitization of government payments. Evidence: [World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project (P180000) PAD](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102502282341480/pdf/P180000048eed6040a13200ddaf8abe650.pdf).
